name: Wisp-Jar
description: A stoppered jar of Isseva pickling-glass, salt water, and a wisp turning in it cold green. It needs no oil and it does not go out. It turns to face whoever is holding it, which most people stop noticing after a week, and some never do.

name: Mother Sundew's Dew
description: A phial of dew off the Mother Sundew in Nelle Saye's tub, clear as gin and odourless. It shuts a wound as glue shuts a crack, and a drop in water is a sleep with no dreams in it.

name: A Named Rope
description: Twenty paces of Hask rope, three strands of reed-hemp and one of eel-skin, with a name walked into it at the wheel and an indigo rag tied at its end. The Hasks say a boat tied with a named rope never drifts.

name: Brannoc Tull's Tally
description: A dredge-master's tally-stick of Guild ash, a notch for every man of the Great Dredge's crew, every notch crossed through at the end in a hand that was not shaking any more. It came off Brannoc Tull's belt at the bottom of the shaft.

name: A Builders' Plate
description: A plate of the Builders' black stone a hand across, cut through with one deep level line and marks either side of it nobody in the Delta can read. It was wired to the dredge-master's tally. The line is the same as the one on the Flood-Mark's needle at Oulea.

name: The Keel-King's Steering-Pin
description: A pin of black Salt Isles iron as long as a forearm, that held the steering-oar to the ship. It is cold and wet whatever you do with it, and it pulls, very slightly, toward the sea.

name: A Ropewalker's Token
description: A ropewalker's token of boxwood on a loop of rope, stamped HASK on the face and cut on the back with a crooked notch. It was on the oarsmen's bench in the Keel-Barrow, where the Salt Isles laid the king's crew, among the bones of a man who was not Salt Isles.

name: Iven Hask's Rope
description: The rope from the rack at Hask's Ropewalk with Iven Hask's own name walked into it nine years ago, for luck, and an indigo rag gone grey. Corra Hask has given it to you to lay at the Keel-Barrow, where his crew musters.

name: The Weavers' Count of Brides
description: A board copied from the weavers' withy tally: the brides walked out, and the night this one turned.

name: Forty Jars
description: The wisp-catcher's count of his jars by number, chalked inside his door and copied out.

name: The Tide-Watchers' Book
description: A tarred book from the box at the gauge's foot: two hundred years of spring tides.

name: The Hask Book of Names
description: The ropewalkers' book of every rope and the name walked into it.

name: A Scrap on the Pole
description: A scrap of indigo cloth from the Unwinding's pole, written on in charcoal.

name: Flights for the Council
description: The heron-reader's book of flights, copied off his slate every evening.

name: The Mother's Feeding
description: The herb-wife's tally of what the Mother Sundew has been fed.

name: The Dredge's Last Shift
description: The Great Dredge's shift-book, in the dredge-master's hand, to its last line, which is in nobody's.

name: The Keel-King's Grave-Roll
description: A driftwood board from among the grave-goods, Salt Isles runes with a reedfolk gloss.
